messages:
Maya: Quick heads-up — got a signal from ACME (pilot) + a public competitor blog today. They shipped a per-route model-mapping control that's resonating with mid-market customers. We should decide whether to chase parity, provide a different angle, or a targeted mitigator. Meeting in 30?

Alex: Thanks for the ping. Can you paste the competitor blurb? want to see exact UX asks.

Maya: https://blog.example.com/fast-routing-models — tl;dr: UI to map routes to cheaper/fast model variants + one-click fallback. Sales says ACME specifically asked for per-customer routing controls.

Sanjay: From ACME: "we want predictable tails and ability to route high-cost requests to backup model automatically." They said they'll delay production if not available. :worried:

Claire: Design thought: we can ship a minimal per-route toggle (toggle + weight slider) and keep advanced routing in next cycle. Minimal would let sales close pilot.

Alex: Engineering reality: minimal toggle + weight slider for routing + new config plumbing across runtime/control-plane ~2 sprints if we reuse existing routing layer. Canary + metrics + rollback hooks are extra. If we push, we risk other planned infra work. Estimate: 2 engineers for 4 wks.

Maya: Proposals to pick from (quick triage):
1) Minimal routing UI + server flag -> ship in 2 sprints (sales-friendly, parity-ish).
2) Docs + recommended pattern + early-access SDK + sales enablement -> buy time, no code change now.
3) Differentiate: lean into "cost-aware routing" with built-in fallback policies + cost SLOs (bigger, 8-10 wks, more strategic).
Please respond with preference + blockers.

Sanjay: I vote for (1) if we can guarantee rollback and an SLA guardrail. Sales needs something tangible.

Alex: I prefer (2) as lowest-risk. If Sales says they will churn without it then (1). We need a clear launch criteria: config validated in staging, E2E latency within 10% of baseline, and automatic fallback tested.

Claire: For (1) launch copy: "Per-route model assignment — map traffic to model variants with instant fallback to protect latency and cost." Needs visuals but we can ship a very small UX.

Maya: Launch criteria draft (for product + eng signoff):
- Feature flag gated in control plane and console.
- End-to-end test covering routing + fallback (automated).
- Observability: per-route token-level cost and P95 latency shown in Console.
- Sales enablement doc + migration playbook.
If we choose (1) I will prioritize design tasks and coordinate an EPD checklist.

Alex: Ok. If we go (1) I need explicit switchover safety: a kill-switch endpoint and metric alarms. Also need a dev-oncall day for rollout.

Sanjay: I'll tell ACME we can aim for a limited pilot if they sign an LOI this month. That helps prioritize.

Maya: Cool — sounds like fast-path (1) is acceptable if Sales secures LOI and Eng gets a small runway. Can each owner ack? @Alex ack if you can commit 2 engs for 4 wks after LOI. @Claire ack design start tomorrow. @Sanjay confirm LOI timeline.

Alex: Ack on conditional commit — need product spec before sprint planning.

Claire: Ack, starting wireframes today.

Sanjay: LOI conversation scheduled for EOD Friday, will update.

ReleaseBot: Meeting created: #roadmap-decision, 2026-03-21 10:00 PT. Invitees: Maya, Alex, Claire, Sanjay. :calendar:
